prompt_instruction: Build the Λ⁰ from the tiles. It is neutral, has baryon number 1 and strangeness −1.
explanation_formal: Λ⁰ = uds: charge +⅔ − ⅓ − ⅓ = 0, baryon number 3 × ⅓ = 1, and strangeness −1 from the s quark. The decoys: ū is an antiquark where a quark belongs, c is the wrong flavour, and a second s would make uss, the Ξ⁰.
explanation_intuitive: Neutral, one strange quark, three quarks in all: u, d, s. A second s overshoots to strangeness −2.
explanation_steps: Baryon number 1 needs three quarks (no antiquarks).
The other two must total charge +⅓: u (+⅔) and d (−⅓).
uds. (Σ⁰ is also uds; the two differ in how the u and d are combined, isospin 0 for Λ versus 1 for Σ⁰.)
source: PDG 2026, Quark Model review §15.2 (quantum numbers); isospin note from Griffiths 2e (chapter to be confirmed)

prompt_instruction: A u quark and an s̄ antiquark. Which hadron is this?
explanation_formal: u s̄ has charge +⅔ + ⅓ = +1 and strangeness +1 (the s̄ carries the opposite of the s quark’s −1). That is the K⁺. The K⁻ is its antiparticle, s ū.
explanation_intuitive: An anti-strange quark gives strangeness +1, and with an up quark the charge is +1: the positive kaon.
explanation_steps: One quark and one antiquark: a meson, colour-neutral.
Charged, S = +1: K⁺. (PDG states it directly: the strangeness of the K⁺ (us̄) is +1.)

prompt_instruction: A u quark and a d quark, on their own. Which hadron is this?
explanation_formal: Two quarks cannot form a colour singlet: a singlet needs a quark with an antiquark, or three quarks. So ud is not a hadron. The π⁺ is u d̄, with an antiquark, which is the trap.
explanation_intuitive: Two colours never add up to neutral. You need a colour and its anticolour, or all three colours.
explanation_steps: Colour-neutral combinations: q q̄ (colour + anticolour) or qqq (one of each colour).
qq is neither. Not a hadron.
Compare π⁺ = u d̄: same flavours, but the d̄ is an antiquark.
